jobs.title: Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications
jobs.description:
Position: Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications

Location: Vaudreuil-Dorion, QC

Flexible Hybrid Work Model: We support collaboration and connection through a hybrid work arrangement requiring a minimum of 3 days per week on-site.

Status: Permanent, full-time (1)

Lead the architecture behind a growing North American business
.

Quadra’s CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience, regulatory compliance and AI platforms are core to how we operate across North America.

We are creating the Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications role to unify these platforms under one architecture and delivery standard. The role leads Quadra Digital’s (QD) Design Authority
pillar alongside Business Authority and Digital Workplace & Infrastructure.

Reporting to our CDIO, this visible, hands-on leader will guide the team, own the budget and investment portfolio, review designs and delivery practices, and partner with business leaders to turn priorities into measurable value.

At Quadra, we put people first so that together, we can reimagine what's possible.

For more than 50 years, Quadra has placed its 650+ employees at the heart of its success across North America. We offer an engaging culture, a collaborative and human environment, and a high level of autonomy and flexibility. Joining Quadra means being part of a professional, innovative and passionate team, within a growing, people-focused organization certified Great Place to Work®. We have also been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for over 20 years.

A leader in the distribution of chemicals and ingredients, Quadra continues to grow with a strong commitment to its teams. If you are driven by excellence, you belong here!

Why This Role Matters

Own enterprise architecture, business capability and process architecture, enterprise information architecture and master data governance, and AI-solution architecture and governance across CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience and AI, as well as Quadra-critical regulatory platforms (Intelligent SDS Authoring, labelling, product stewardship and compliance).
Lead the platform managers, product owners, delivery squads, project management and QA under one intake and delivery model.
Enforce design, security, testing and release standards to make delivery predictable.
Own the digital budget and investment portfolio with Finance, the CDIO and business leaders.
Measure digital outcomes through revenue, margin, cost, service, working capital and productivity.

What would be your main responsibilities as Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications?:

Define and govern target architecture across applications, integrations, data, security and AI; approve major designs, configurations, developments and releases.
Directly manage the platform managers, product owners, project management, QA, development and functional specialists—setting priorities, capacity, performance and development expectations.
Own delivery from qualified demand through release and Level 3 support, including application security, published SLAs and clear technical ownership.
Set and enforce delivery standards for requirements, backlogs, acceptance criteria, UAT, Jira, testing and Definition of Done.
Bring the roadmap and enhancement portfolio to the quarterly QD Prioritisation Board and provide technical validation for production changes.
Map business capabilities, processes and applications to align investments, reduce duplication and challenge proposed solutions early.
Evaluate AI and regulatory platforms (e.g., SDS authoring, labelling, product stewardship) against security, compliance, integration, data and business-value requirements.
Own digital opex and capex planning, business-case quality, stage gates and value realization with Finance, Business Authority and the relevant Key Account.
Advise business leaders on roadmap, feasibility, cost and sequencing; lead vendor selection and performance management.
Assess and integrate application landscapes acquired through mergers and acquisitions.

What are the required qualifications and experience to succeed in this role:

15+ years in enterprise/solution architecture, application management or digital delivery, including 5+ years leading specialists or Product Owners.
Bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, software or industrial engineering, or equivalent experience.
Proven design-authority experience across multiple platforms, including solution, integration and release approvals.
Hands-on experience with at least two of: Salesforce, Oracle JD Edwards E1 or similar ERP, Oracle OTM/TMS
Strong integration and API architecture experience across ERP, CRM and TMS in cloud or hybrid environments.
Strong business acumen and ability to translate commercial, operational and financial priorities into practical technology decisions.
Strong oral presentation skills: clear, confident communication of complex ideas, analysis outcomes, architectural concepts and design decisions—and their justification—tailored to diverse audiences and stakeholder needs.
Experience governing requirements, backlogs, Jira or Azure DevOps, SDLC controls, change management, segregation of duties and audit/compliance reviews.
Demonstrated creative thinking and ability to challenge stakeholders, defend decisions, bring stakeholders to understand and accept new approaches and deliver measurable business benefits.
Proven experience owning and managing significant technology operating and capital budgets and investment portfolios, in partnership with Finance and business leaders, with accountability for forecasting, prioritization, cost control and value realization.
Advanced written and verbal communication skills in both French and English.
Assets: MuleSoft or similar API integration platform experience; TOGAF, Zachman, AWS/Azure, Microsoft Power Platform, Power BI/Fabric, Agile/SAFe or Scrum certification; distribution, chemicals, supply chain, regulatory/product stewardship or post-acquisition integration experience.

Working Conditions

Permanent, full-time senior leadership role based in Vaudreuil-Dorion, with three full office days per week.
Travel up to 15% across Canada and the United States.
Occasional off-hours involvement for major releases, incidents or critical business events.

You Might Be the Right Person If…

You are a pragmatic, hands-on leader who can review architecture, lead a team and own a budget. You set standards appropriate for a 650-person company, enforce them without becoming a bottleneck, challenge unclear value and hold delivery accountable for measurable results.

We want to meet you!

Here Are Some Of The Perks Of Choosing Quadra

Permanent, full-time leadership opportunity: Join a growing organization where you can make a meaningful impact and help shape future success.
Competitive compensation & performance incentives: We recognize and reward strong performance with a competitive salary and incentive program.
Lead with impact: Partner with talented teams and contribute to strategic initiatives that drive business growth and operational excellence.
Comprehensive benefits package: Medical, dental, healthcare spending account, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and access to virtual healthcare.
Retirement savings program: Build for the future with our matched pension plan.
Flexible time off: Vacation, personal days, and wellness initiatives that support work-life balance.
Professional growth opportunities: Expand your leadership capabilities through challenging projects, cross-functional collaboration, and ongoing development.
Values-driven culture: Be part of a collaborative organization built on integrity, accountability, entrepreneurship, and care for people.
Family-owned with long-term vision: Enjoy the stability of a privately owned company that takes a long-term approach to investing in its people and business.
Award-winning workplace: Proudly recognized as a Great Place to Work® and one of Canada's Best Managed Companies.
Inclusive and collaborative environment: We value diverse perspectives and foster a culture where people can thrive and contribute.
Community involvement: Participate in volunteer and community initiatives that make a positive impact.
Recognition and appreciation: Celebrate achievements through our recognition programs and culture of acknowledgment.
And much more!

Compensation Information:
The annual base pay range for this position is reasonably expected to be $135,000.000 to $205,000.00. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is only a part of the total rewards package - this role will also be eligible for a generous incentive program and benefits. Quadra’s salary ranges are benchmarked and are determined by role and level. Please note that the base pay shown qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location.

At Quadra, we are committed to offering a competitive and rewarding compensation package that recognizes your expertise, contributions, and professional growth.

In accordance with Quebec's Charter of the French Language (Bill 101), proficiency in French is required for this position. Given the nature of the role and the frequent interactions with colleagues, customers, and business partners across Canada and internationally, advanced English language skills are also required.

#quadra1

Quadra supports and values diversity and offer equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status and gender identity. Quadra also welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. We recognize that some people do not identify themselves as either male or female. Therefore, whenever possible, we have opted for a gender-neutral wording in a non-discriminatory spirit.

Please note that Quadra recruiters only use official @quadragroup.com email addresses. We never request fees or sensitive personal information during recruitment. Be cautious if you receive messages from domains that look similar to Quadra Group but are not official. If in doubt, please contact us directly via our Careers page.

jobs.title: Director, GTM Planning & Compensation
jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.
Fluency in Salesforce data and at least one planning or ICM platform.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions to be in office minimum twice per week. (Find your Hub)
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The on-target earnings (OTE) salary range for this role is $207,400 to $311,000 reflecting base salary plus variable compensation at 100% attainment. Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

We're a Human and High Performing AI company, meaning we use artificial intelligence to improve all of our operations. In recruitment, AI helps us streamline the process for greater efficiency. However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

Description

Why This Role Exists

Creative is one of the biggest levers in scaling our clients’ paid media performance.

We’re looking for a Head of Creative Strategy to build the people, systems, and operating model that turn creative into a repeatable performance advantage across our portfolio, both in social and display networks.

You’ll lead Creative Strategy and oversee Creative Execution through the Performance Creative Manager, ensuring strategy, production, performance, and learning operate as one connected system.

Key Responsibilities

Who We Are

Clever Digital Marketing is a performance marketing agency helping large home improvement companies across the US and Canada grow through Paid Social, Paid Search, CRO, and strategic advising.

We manage a large portfolio of accounts, an in-house creative team, and significant monthly ad spend. As we scale, we're building a stronger creative-strategy function to help clients find new creative winners — and to turn one-off learnings into repeatable systems that compound across every account.

Skills, Knowledge And Expertise

What You'll Do

Build and lead CDM’s Creative Strategy function, defining the methodologies, standards, and operating system behind how we research, ideate, test, learn, and scale creative.
Manage Senior Creative Strategists and the Performance Creative Manager.
Build systems that turn customer, market, and performance data into actionable creative direction.
Create a cross-account learning system so wins, losses, hypotheses, and insights compound across the portfolio.
Set and maintain the strategic and creative quality bar across the department, regularly reviewing work and challenging thinking.
Ensure Creative Strategy and Creative Execution scale together with the right quality, capacity, velocity, prioritization, and feedback loops.
Build testing frameworks, briefing standards, and learning loops that improve creative performance and decision-making.
Build training, playbooks, and frameworks that improve creative thinking across Media Buyers and Creative.
Build AI-enabled workflows that improve research, analysis, creative intelligence, and decision-making.
Partner closely with Paid Social, CRO, Paid Search, Client Success, and leadership.
Ensure creative decisions are connected to business outcomes such as Creative Win Rate, CPL, CPS/CPD, lead quality, COM, and account growth.
Hire and develop future Creative Strategy talent.

What We’re Looking For

Proven experience leading creative strategy or performance creative.
Experience building or scaling a team, department, or operating system.
Strong performance-marketing and commercial understanding.
Strong direct-response and consumer-psychology background.
Experience building creative testing frameworks, learning systems, and standards.
Experience managing strategists and/or creative-production teams.
Strong cross-functional leadership and ability to drive adoption.
Strong understanding of AI and how to apply it across a team, not just individually.
Able to operate at portfolio level while still maintaining a strong account-level creative quality bar.
Clear, decisive communicator who can simplify complexity and turn strategy into action.

Nice to Have

Lead generation or high-ticket services experience.
Home improvement experience.
CRO and landing-page testing familiarity.
UGC, founder-led, or spokesperson-led creative experience.
Hands-on familiarity with editing or design tools.

What Success Looks Like

CDM consistently introduces genuinely new creative ideas instead of recycling the same concepts and formats.
Creative iterations are more deliberate, strategic, and evidence-based.
Media Buyers and editors produce stronger briefs and creative recommendations on their own.
Learnings are captured, shared, and applied across accounts.
AI-supported research and creative workflows are adopted department-wide.
CDM has a repeatable creative-strategy engine that gets stronger with every test.

Benefits

Benefits of Working at CDM

Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses
Flexible remote work environment with option for in-person collaboration (Vaughan, ON)
Group Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision, RRSP/401k Plan w/matching, more.
Company-provided MacBook computer
Home office budget and Clever merch delivery to get you started
Work Abroad Policy: Need a new working environment? Our work abroad policy supports this!
The chance to shape and grow a high-performing Client Success team
A culture of performance and respect where the best work happens with extreme ownership and accountability meets collaboration.

Clever Digital Marketing values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the team. At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Build more than a career – help shape what comes next

The Argus Group of Companies is seeking a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join its senior leadership team. This is a key leadership role for an accomplished finance executive who can bring together financial strategy, capital planning, development and investment analysis, and strong financial governance to a dynamic group. Working closely with ownership and the executive team, the CFO will help guide strategic decision-making, strengthen financial performance, and position the organization for continued growth across its portfolio.

More than a real estate company, Argus is a diversified, entrepreneurial group that has been helping shape the Okanagan for more than 50 years. Headquartered in Kelowna, British Columbia, Argus has built an impressive portfolio spanning commercial, residential, industrial and hospitality properties, supported by in-house expertise across hospitality management, development, construction, leasing and property management

What makes Argus particularly compelling is its long-term approach to ownership. Rather than simply developing properties and moving on, the organization invests, develops, operates and manages assets with a view to creating enduring value. That means its leaders have the opportunity to be involved across the full property lifecycle and to see the tangible, lasting impact of the decisions they make.

This is a place where good ideas can move quickly, leaders are close to the decisions that matter, and your work can leave a visible legacy. As Argus looks toward its next phase of growth, it offers something increasingly rare: the chance to join a successful organization and still have a genuine hand in shaping its future

Key Responsibilities

Shape organizational and growth strategy – Serve as a trusted leader and advisor to ownership, bringing financial insight, commercial judgement and constructive challenge to major business and investment decisions
Lead capital and financing strategy – Drive long-term capital planning, financing and refinancing, liquidity management and lender relationships, supported by robust forecasting and scenario modelling to provide clear visibility into cash flow, leverage and capital requirements and optimize the capital structure to support sustainable growth.
Evaluate investments and growth opportunities – Lead the financial assessment of developments, acquisitions and major capital investments, evaluating returns, cash flow, funding requirements, risk and long-term value creation.
Optimize capital deployment – Advise ownership on where and how to deploy capital across new developments, acquisitions, existing assets, property improvements and debt reduction.
Strengthen portfolio performance – Assess asset and business-line performance and work with development and operational leaders to enhance returns, cash generation and long-term portfolio value.
Manage financial and enterprise risk – Maintain a forward-looking view of liquidity, leverage, debt maturities, interest-rate exposure, project risk and market conditions, ensuring appropriate financial governance and controls.
Build trusted financial relationships – Develop strong relationships with banks, lenders, investors and external financial partners, expanding access to capital and supporting future opportunities.
Turn strategy into action – Translate complex financial information into clear, commercially grounded recommendations, combining strategic leadership with a practical, hands-on approach to execution.
Build finance capability for the future – Lead and develop a strong finance team, ensuring the function continues to evolve in step with the increasing scale, complexity and ambitions of the organization.
Help shape what comes next – Take on other strategic priorities and opportunities where financial leadership, commercial judgement and a hands-on approach can add value.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, accounting, commerce, or a related discipline.
Professional accounting designation (CPA), required.
Master of Business Administration (MBA) or other post-graduate considered an asset.
15+ years of progressive experience, including senior financial leadership experience.
Strong experience in real estate development, property management, corporate finance, or related industry, with demonstrated expertise in financing, debt structuring, and lender relationships.
Proven ability to advise ownership and executive leadership on strategic financial decisions.

Skills & Attributes

Curious and Imaginative –
Energized by building, growing, and shaping the future of the group.
Influential and collaborative –
Leads through influence, collaboration, sound judgement, and accountability.
Commercially astute –
Identifies opportunities, solves problems, and creates value.
Entrepreneurial –

new_jobs.description:
Position: Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications

Location: Vaudreuil-Dorion, QC

Flexible Hybrid Work Model: We support collaboration and connection through a hybrid work arrangement requiring a minimum of 3 days per week on-site.

Status: Permanent, full-time (1)

Lead the architecture behind a growing North American business
.

Quadra’s CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience, regulatory compliance and AI platforms are core to how we operate across North America.

We are creating the Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications role to unify these platforms under one architecture and delivery standard. The role leads Quadra Digital’s (QD) Design Authority
pillar alongside Business Authority and Digital Workplace & Infrastructure.

Reporting to our CDIO, this visible, hands-on leader will guide the team, own the budget and investment portfolio, review designs and delivery practices, and partner with business leaders to turn priorities into measurable value.

At Quadra, we put people first so that together, we can reimagine what's possible.

For more than 50 years, Quadra has placed its 650+ employees at the heart of its success across North America. We offer an engaging culture, a collaborative and human environment, and a high level of autonomy and flexibility. Joining Quadra means being part of a professional, innovative and passionate team, within a growing, people-focused organization certified Great Place to Work®. We have also been recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies for over 20 years.

A leader in the distribution of chemicals and ingredients, Quadra continues to grow with a strong commitment to its teams. If you are driven by excellence, you belong here!

Why This Role Matters

Own enterprise architecture, business capability and process architecture, enterprise information architecture and master data governance, and AI-solution architecture and governance across CRM, ERP, transportation, analytics, employee experience and AI, as well as Quadra-critical regulatory platforms (Intelligent SDS Authoring, labelling, product stewardship and compliance).
Lead the platform managers, product owners, delivery squads, project management and QA under one intake and delivery model.
Enforce design, security, testing and release standards to make delivery predictable.
Own the digital budget and investment portfolio with Finance, the CDIO and business leaders.
Measure digital outcomes through revenue, margin, cost, service, working capital and productivity.

What would be your main responsibilities as Head of Enterprise Architecture & Applications?:

Define and govern target architecture across applications, integrations, data, security and AI; approve major designs, configurations, developments and releases.
Directly manage the platform managers, product owners, project management, QA, development and functional specialists—setting priorities, capacity, performance and development expectations.
Own delivery from qualified demand through release and Level 3 support, including application security, published SLAs and clear technical ownership.
Set and enforce delivery standards for requirements, backlogs, acceptance criteria, UAT, Jira, testing and Definition of Done.
Bring the roadmap and enhancement portfolio to the quarterly QD Prioritisation Board and provide technical validation for production changes.
Map business capabilities, processes and applications to align investments, reduce duplication and challenge proposed solutions early.
Evaluate AI and regulatory platforms (e.g., SDS authoring, labelling, product stewardship) against security, compliance, integration, data and business-value requirements.
Own digital opex and capex planning, business-case quality, stage gates and value realization with Finance, Business Authority and the relevant Key Account.
Advise business leaders on roadmap, feasibility, cost and sequencing; lead vendor selection and performance management.
Assess and integrate application landscapes acquired through mergers and acquisitions.

What are the required qualifications and experience to succeed in this role:

15+ years in enterprise/solution architecture, application management or digital delivery, including 5+ years leading specialists or Product Owners.
Bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, software or industrial engineering, or equivalent experience.
Proven design-authority experience across multiple platforms, including solution, integration and release approvals.
Hands-on experience with at least two of: Salesforce, Oracle JD Edwards E1 or similar ERP, Oracle OTM/TMS
Strong integration and API architecture experience across ERP, CRM and TMS in cloud or hybrid environments.
Strong business acumen and ability to translate commercial, operational and financial priorities into practical technology decisions.
Strong oral presentation skills: clear, confident communication of complex ideas, analysis outcomes, architectural concepts and design decisions—and their justification—tailored to diverse audiences and stakeholder needs.
Experience governing requirements, backlogs, Jira or Azure DevOps, SDLC controls, change management, segregation of duties and audit/compliance reviews.
Demonstrated creative thinking and ability to challenge stakeholders, defend decisions, bring stakeholders to understand and accept new approaches and deliver measurable business benefits.
Proven experience owning and managing significant technology operating and capital budgets and investment portfolios, in partnership with Finance and business leaders, with accountability for forecasting, prioritization, cost control and value realization.
Advanced written and verbal communication skills in both French and English.
Assets: MuleSoft or similar API integration platform experience; TOGAF, Zachman, AWS/Azure, Microsoft Power Platform, Power BI/Fabric, Agile/SAFe or Scrum certification; distribution, chemicals, supply chain, regulatory/product stewardship or post-acquisition integration experience.

Working Conditions

Permanent, full-time senior leadership role based in Vaudreuil-Dorion, with three full office days per week.
Travel up to 15% across Canada and the United States.
Occasional off-hours involvement for major releases, incidents or critical business events.

You Might Be the Right Person If…

You are a pragmatic, hands-on leader who can review architecture, lead a team and own a budget. You set standards appropriate for a 650-person company, enforce them without becoming a bottleneck, challenge unclear value and hold delivery accountable for measurable results.

We want to meet you!

Here Are Some Of The Perks Of Choosing Quadra

Permanent, full-time leadership opportunity: Join a growing organization where you can make a meaningful impact and help shape future success.
Competitive compensation & performance incentives: We recognize and reward strong performance with a competitive salary and incentive program.
Lead with impact: Partner with talented teams and contribute to strategic initiatives that drive business growth and operational excellence.
Comprehensive benefits package: Medical, dental, healthcare spending account, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and access to virtual healthcare.
Retirement savings program: Build for the future with our matched pension plan.
Flexible time off: Vacation, personal days, and wellness initiatives that support work-life balance.
Professional growth opportunities: Expand your leadership capabilities through challenging projects, cross-functional collaboration, and ongoing development.
Values-driven culture: Be part of a collaborative organization built on integrity, accountability, entrepreneurship, and care for people.
Family-owned with long-term vision: Enjoy the stability of a privately owned company that takes a long-term approach to investing in its people and business.
Award-winning workplace: Proudly recognized as a Great Place to Work® and one of Canada's Best Managed Companies.
Inclusive and collaborative environment: We value diverse perspectives and foster a culture where people can thrive and contribute.
Community involvement: Participate in volunteer and community initiatives that make a positive impact.
Recognition and appreciation: Celebrate achievements through our recognition programs and culture of acknowledgment.
And much more!

Compensation Information:
The annual base pay range for this position is reasonably expected to be $135,000.000 to $205,000.00. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is only a part of the total rewards package - this role will also be eligible for a generous incentive program and benefits. Quadra’s salary ranges are benchmarked and are determined by role and level. Please note that the base pay shown qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location.

At Quadra, we are committed to offering a competitive and rewarding compensation package that recognizes your expertise, contributions, and professional growth.

In accordance with Quebec's Charter of the French Language (Bill 101), proficiency in French is required for this position. Given the nature of the role and the frequent interactions with colleagues, customers, and business partners across Canada and internationally, advanced English language skills are also required.

Description

Why This Role Exists

Creative is one of the biggest levers in scaling our clients’ paid media performance.

We’re looking for a Head of Creative Strategy to build the people, systems, and operating model that turn creative into a repeatable performance advantage across our portfolio, both in social and display networks.

You’ll lead Creative Strategy and oversee Creative Execution through the Performance Creative Manager, ensuring strategy, production, performance, and learning operate as one connected system.

Key Responsibilities

Who We Are

Clever Digital Marketing is a performance marketing agency helping large home improvement companies across the US and Canada grow through Paid Social, Paid Search, CRO, and strategic advising.

We manage a large portfolio of accounts, an in-house creative team, and significant monthly ad spend. As we scale, we're building a stronger creative-strategy function to help clients find new creative winners — and to turn one-off learnings into repeatable systems that compound across every account.

Skills, Knowledge And Expertise

What You'll Do

Build and lead CDM’s Creative Strategy function, defining the methodologies, standards, and operating system behind how we research, ideate, test, learn, and scale creative.
Manage Senior Creative Strategists and the Performance Creative Manager.
Build systems that turn customer, market, and performance data into actionable creative direction.
Create a cross-account learning system so wins, losses, hypotheses, and insights compound across the portfolio.
Set and maintain the strategic and creative quality bar across the department, regularly reviewing work and challenging thinking.
Ensure Creative Strategy and Creative Execution scale together with the right quality, capacity, velocity, prioritization, and feedback loops.
Build testing frameworks, briefing standards, and learning loops that improve creative performance and decision-making.
Build training, playbooks, and frameworks that improve creative thinking across Media Buyers and Creative.
Build AI-enabled workflows that improve research, analysis, creative intelligence, and decision-making.
Partner closely with Paid Social, CRO, Paid Search, Client Success, and leadership.
Ensure creative decisions are connected to business outcomes such as Creative Win Rate, CPL, CPS/CPD, lead quality, COM, and account growth.
Hire and develop future Creative Strategy talent.

What We’re Looking For

Proven experience leading creative strategy or performance creative.
Experience building or scaling a team, department, or operating system.
Strong performance-marketing and commercial understanding.
Strong direct-response and consumer-psychology background.
Experience building creative testing frameworks, learning systems, and standards.
Experience managing strategists and/or creative-production teams.
Strong cross-functional leadership and ability to drive adoption.
Strong understanding of AI and how to apply it across a team, not just individually.
Able to operate at portfolio level while still maintaining a strong account-level creative quality bar.
Clear, decisive communicator who can simplify complexity and turn strategy into action.

Nice to Have

Lead generation or high-ticket services experience.
Home improvement experience.
CRO and landing-page testing familiarity.
UGC, founder-led, or spokesperson-led creative experience.
Hands-on familiarity with editing or design tools.

What Success Looks Like

CDM consistently introduces genuinely new creative ideas instead of recycling the same concepts and formats.
Creative iterations are more deliberate, strategic, and evidence-based.
Media Buyers and editors produce stronger briefs and creative recommendations on their own.
Learnings are captured, shared, and applied across accounts.
AI-supported research and creative workflows are adopted department-wide.
CDM has a repeatable creative-strategy engine that gets stronger with every test.

Benefits

Benefits of Working at CDM

Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses
Flexible remote work environment with option for in-person collaboration (Vaughan, ON)
Group Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision, RRSP/401k Plan w/matching, more.
Company-provided MacBook computer
Home office budget and Clever merch delivery to get you started
Work Abroad Policy: Need a new working environment? Our work abroad policy supports this!
The chance to shape and grow a high-performing Client Success team
A culture of performance and respect where the best work happens with extreme ownership and accountability meets collaboration.

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible
